title: Agent work on every page: sanity checks, consensus, the page drawer

message.text:
The design is up: [design.md](/framework/ai/2026/09/28/agent-work-on-every-page-sanity-checks-c/design.md), one picture and one table. Every page is a context with a ☰ menu at the top right. The menu opens the drawer, which has AI, Sessions, Dictation, Settings and Admin tabs, and each page has its own fast assistant and manager. Two cheap checkers look at every decision; when they disagree, 5 models at 3 prices vote. ext/Research stays for real research programs only.

Ready to dispatch, in order:
A) role `task-mastermind`, name `page-drawer`, `claude-opus-5-5`, medium, `bypassPermissions`, brief ai/2026-09-28/page-drawer/requirements.md.
B) recursive-pairs (dispatch.md row #2), which now includes the idle-agent lifecycle and a pair for any page. It can run beside A.
C) role `task-mastermind`, name `check-consensus`, `claude-sonnet-5`, medium, `bypassPermissions`, brief ai/2026-09-28/check-consensus/requirements.md, after fresh-eyes review lands.
D) OpenRouter models and web search in the checks: part of harness steps 1–2, noted in architect-review.md.
Use the standard prompt for each: "You own one task. Your brief is <brief>… Post progress on card 2026/09/28/agent-work-on-every-page-sanity-checks-c, two sentences at a time."
Taken: building check() (2 fresh checkers) and consensus() from the fresh-eyes-review spawn pattern, plus the docs and proof runs the brief asks for. Working in my own worktree.

The design now has one collaboration system for research, planning and design ([design.md](/framework/ai/2026/09/28/agent-work-on-every-page-sanity-checks-c/design.md), the "Added" section). Six objects: Collab, Member, Phase, Vote with a caveat, Source and Lesson. The rounds go: brief, read peers, revise, vote. Object-oriented design votes in stages, names first. The web fan-out saves each source as markdown once in `sources/`. Docs use one convention, `doc/`: `/docs/` URLs redirect there, and nested markdown shows as a browsable tree.

For task-mastermind-check-consensus: keep your scope, and give votes the shape {member, pick, caveat} so collab-rounds can reuse it.

Ready to dispatch: #10 role `task-mastermind`, name `collab-rounds`, `claude-opus-5-5`, medium, `bypassPermissions`, brief ai/2026-09-28/collab-rounds/requirements.md. #11 role `task-mastermind`, name `source-library`, `claude-sonnet-5`, medium, `bypassPermissions`, brief ai/2026-09-28/source-library/requirements.md. They can run side by side.

Collab rounds started: two builders are at work, one on the objects and the page that draws a run, one on the runner that takes agents through the rounds. Next come two real runs, one research and one design vote, each with its cost.

Taken: task #11, the source library — public/framework/sources/, Server/sources.mjs's web fan-out, the doc/docs nesting fix, and the research skill's lesson rule. Spinning up my own worktree, then splitting into minions per fenced piece.

Taken: the inbox workspace. A builder is trying the opened card as a whole page with its own left nav, centred, behind a workspace toggle that is off by default, so your current view stays as it is. The layout is one shared piece the page mastermind will reuse. Also: a documented content.js per card, with one example card. Screenshots at 1920 and 3440 come here.

check() and consensus() are built and committed; fresh-eyes review flagged real cost (measured ~$0.18/check, ~$0.47/consensus vs $0.01/$0.05 targets — likely fixable, a per-turn CLAUDE.md/skill-listing tax) and two real bugs. Fixing those now, then running the proof (5 real decisions + 1 real open question) before landing.

The runner works: a test with two Haiku agents went through all four rounds and a vote for $0.32, and most of that was each agent's startup cost. Two real runs with three agents each are going now: a research run on which consensus method works best, and a staged design vote on the Source class.

Split into three minions in one worktree: doc-tree (nested notes + /docs/→/doc/ redirect, kept out of Router.js), sources-lib (the sources/ library shape, Server/sources.mjs fan-out, its page, and a real seed run against three topics), research-skill-lesson (one section in the research skill). All three are working now; I'll review, review.mjs, smoke-test and merge once they land.

Fixed a snag: my task-dir briefs weren't visible inside the shared worktree until I copied them over. All three minions are unblocked now; the research-skill one drafted its section but hit some blocker applying the edit — chasing that down now.

The research run ($1.92) came back with a clear answer: a plain vote of about five agents, with one read-and-revise round only when the vote is close, beats debate on cost. The design run ($1.56) got the names vote right but miscounted the second vote, so the runner is being fixed and a clean design vote on the Scoreboard class runs after that.

Ready to try: the inbox workspace. Press the small WORKSPACE word at the top of the inbox (or add ?view=workspace), and an opened card becomes a whole page with its own left nav (its tabs and sub-cards), centred in the space; the chat stays on the right. Your current view is unchanged while it is off. Try it: /framework/ai2/2026/09/24/system-design/?view=workspace . Pictures: 3440 on /framework/ai/2026-09-28/ai2-workspace/shots/ai2w-system-design-3440-on.png , 3440 off /framework/ai/2026-09-28/ai2-workspace/shots/ai2w-system-design-3440-off.png . Also: any card can now draw anything with a content.js in its folder; the example card imports two site modules: /framework/ai2/2026/09/28/example-a-card-s-content-js/ . The layout is one shared piece, ai2/floating.js, which the page mastermind will reuse as its Floating page layout.

Landed one of four pieces (the research-skill lesson rule). Found a real snag: both remaining minions were spawned under a permission mode that silently blocked every node/bash command — fixed by resuming them with full permissions, now queued behind other memory-hungry agents on the machine. sources-lib had already written its files (script, page, docs) before hitting the wall; doc-tree was mid-edit.

Facts first, disputes and abstaining are a small follow-up to collab, kept separate so review-turns stays small. Every collab now opens by listing its facts ("always X", "one A per B", "before X, do Y"), each marked settled, likely or open. Open facts are where the digging goes. Any member may dispute a fact with one line saying why, and a vote can be an abstention, which isn't counted for anything. "Always" and "never" are only for what actually breaks.

Ready to dispatch #14: role `task-mastermind`, name `collab-facts`, `claude-sonnet-5`, medium, `bypassPermissions`, brief ai/2026-09-28/collab-facts/requirements.md, after review-turns lands.

Page drawer, taken: one minion is building the ☰ menu and the drawer's five routed tabs (AI, Sessions, Dictation, Settings, Admin) in its own worktree. Next, a second minion makes any paragraph or card selectable, with its properties in the drawer and a chip that adds it to the page chat.

The runner now counts every vote. Doc pages have a ⋯ after any method name that a vote chose, which opens that decision. A clean staged design vote on the Scoreboard class is running on the fixed runner now, and its result gives the first real ⋯ link.

The ☰ menu and the drawer's five tabs are built and proven in screenshots, and not merged yet. From the Sessions tab, an old Ask thread was reopened and remembered its conversation. Now the same minion is making any paragraph or card selectable, with a chip that adds it to the chat.

Collab rounds landed: three cheap agents work a question in rounds and vote with caveats, and /framework/ext/Collab/ draws every decision with all its alternatives. On a doc page, the ⋯ after a name the agents chose opens that decision (see Scoreboard.retire). A real design vote cost $2.03 and a research run $1.92. The merge is in the main tree's working files, waiting for you to commit it, and your overrule click is built but hasn't been tried yet.

Landed on michael/dev: the source library at /framework/sources/ (3 real topics seeded, $0.85 total), Server/sources.mjs's fan-out + cite tool, a research-skill rule for where lessons go, and /docs/ now resolving to /doc/ with a real nested doc tree (proven 3 deep) in ext/Doc. Two full fresh-eyes reviews, 9 findings fixed/declined with reasons, all live-verified at 1920. It landed alongside a sibling task editing the same Doc.js concurrently — caught and recovered one bad conflict-resolution step mid-way (their uncommitted work, briefly discarded, restored exactly) before the real merge went through clean. Full report in the task log.

The ☰ drawer is now on the live site: its tabs, element selection and the context chip, and a reload on ?drawer=sessions lands on Sessions. One bug is being fixed: the home page's clock band goes blank when the drawer opens as the page loads.
Taken: Fact object + facts-first phase, disputes, and abstaining for collab-rounds. Working in a worktree off michael/dev.

Landed: every page has a ☰ drawer with AI, Sessions, Dictation, Settings and Admin tabs. Click any paragraph or card to see its properties and ask about it. The walkthrough is seven Next clicks: /framework/ext/drawer/walkthrough/. The blank clock is ext/Panel's own (blank for up to a second on every load), and the card's bottom chat box is still AI 2's to remove.
Progress: the minion has Collab.js, collab.mjs, view.js and collab.css all in progress in its worktree (Fact object, facts phase, disputes, abstain). Still building — no commit yet.

Landed: collab-facts is live on michael/dev. Every collab run now starts with a Facts phase (settled/likely/open certainty), lets any member dispute a fact later, and lets a vote abstain — proven free via mock and with three real paid runs (one of which found and fixed a real bug). Details: /framework/ai/2026-09-28/collab-facts/task.jsonl
